AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If
 you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the
 City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  APRIL 20, 2021

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale City Council meeting will be available to the public
electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  City Attorney Mike Garcia indicated that action is anticipated. For the record and
  purpose of the Minutes, the matter that is in Closed Session Agenda related to a
  potential litigation pertains to a dispute between the City of Glendale and Glendale
  Community College (GCC) regarding the applicability of the standby rate to a fuel
  cell project proposed by GCC and a conflict waiver related there to. Council
  recessed to Closed Session at 4:48 p.m.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Public Information Officer Eliza Papazian announced the 20th Annual Armenian Genocide
  Virtual Event, to be held on April 24.

  Council Member Agajanian was disappointed on the outcome of the Special Council
  Meeting today regarding the decision in response to the city’s request to negotiate a lease
  and management agreement for the Alex Theatre.

  Council Member Brotman thanked Council for starting the AGZA and asked staff for a
  complete implementation across all of the city’s parks and other city site to use gas-powered

  04 20 21
  CC
   landscaping equipment and eventually roll-out to the community at large. He talked about AB-
  1346: Air Pollution – small off-road engines. He commended the Glendale Environmental
  Coalition for doing a street clean-up on Earth Day.

  Council Member Kassakhian spoke about having a volunteer group to come together to
  clean-up streets. He also asked staff to empty overflowing trash cans around the city. He
  asked staff to install shades and benches on bus stops that is frequented by commuters.
  Brotman seconded. Kassakhian reminded staff to provide the packets and reports for the
  upcoming Tuesday meetings to be sent to them immediately as discussed and adopted in
  previous meetings.

  Council Member Najarian provided a brief report on Metro Transit’s programs.

  Mayor Devine attended the Glendale Education Foundation Fundraiser and commended
  Director of IPA Elena Bolbolian for receiving the Diamond Award for outstanding
  accomplishments. She shared to Council that she had received gratitude from employees of
  Vons and Ralph’s for approving the “Hero Pay Ordinance.” She attended the soft opening of
  the Jewel Vaccine Clinic. Fire Chief Silvio Lanzas provided a brief update on the COVID
  vaccine. She announced a virtual event on April 27 on Race to Zero Emission. Mrs. Devine
  asked staff to draft a letter of support to Cong. Schiff in support of the US House Resolution
  demanding Azerbaijan to release all Armenian hostages. Agajanian seconded. Lastly, she
  announced there is a Pop-Up Art Exhibit on Artsakh Avenue and presented a Commendation
  to “She Loves Collective” in recognition of their interactive installation of “My Relic: a
  contemporary view of the Armenian Culture.”
